tools.note: resource counts are toolchain-sensitive; a toolchain bump is expected to move them and should re-lock deliberately

tolerance.note: logic may drift a few percent with synthesis changes, but BSRAM and DSP counts are structural and must be exact; fmax must stay within 3% and above 25 MHz

runtime.note: loader-only: blank RAM, immutable UART ROM, no baked program. This is the bitstream a board should be running, and the one every shipped payload (games, examples, kernels) executes on, so it is locked instead of a per-program row. It costs about 1,534 LUT4 more than a baked image (13,891 for the same profile carrying snake) because axrom reads combinationally and cannot map to BSRAM; 20 BSRAMs are free if that is ever changed.

ax2.note: known failure: 110% LUT4, overflows the device. Recorded as failing rather than redefined; making it fit requires dropping branch prediction, which changes what it measures. A build that starts passing is also a baseline violation and must be re-locked deliberately.

provenance.runtime: in-tree build 2026-08-10: make fpga-loader-primer, seed 1, routed fmax (not the post-placement estimate)
provenance.tpu: in-tree rebuild after the 77553a2 regression fix; the sweep predates that fix and recorded tpu as failing

known_stale_rows.gpu-lane1: Locked from the sweep at 12,281 LUT4 / 33.61 MHz. A current build measures 13,393 / 35.73 because sw/baremetal/examples/gpu_lane1.c gained volatile reference arrays after that sweep ran. Re-lock from a fresh sweep.
known_stale_rows.morph-1pe: Same situation: sw/baremetal/examples/morph.c changed after the sweep. The in-tree build that was loaded on the board measured 20,176 / 29.20 against the locked 19,158 / 32.01.
known_stale_rows.note: These two rows will flag on the next sweep. That is the gate working, not a hardware problem; re-lock them deliberately once a post-fix sweep exists.
